$comment: Divergence registry for the lnwjud-x fork of https://github.com/engasnm111/lnwjud.
Every entry is a behaviour this repository added that the upstream project does not have and
therefore has no reason to preserve. A merge from upstream can delete it while still merging
cleanly, so each entry names the source marker that proves it survived plus the test that
actually exercises it. tests/release/upstream-divergence.test.ts fails if any marker disappears.
Add an entry here whenever lnwjud-x changes upstream-owned behaviour. Do not add upstream-owned

customizations.summary: The fork's sync commands and the release-gate registration of its guard tests live in the root package.json. Resolving that file as version noise during a merge deletes the commands and silently drops upstream-divergence and native-active-project-wiring from test:release-gate, so the guard stops running while CI still reports green.
An absolute path outside every Active Project is attached as a project by the host instead of being refused with 'not registered'.
Path routing and native path-scope enforcement read one shared key list, so no path field can be enforced without also being routable.

A refusal an assistant will repeat to the user names the retry that actually works and states only constraints the code really enforces. A vague scope refusal made assistants tell the user to register the folder by hand, or claim the host cannot read the path at all when the batch merely spanned two projects. The image branch of media_read separately answered 'action=inspect only' while it accepts inspect and frame identically, so callers were told a false limitation and retried it; the denial now names both accepted actions and echoes the rejected one.

markers.contains: Image media supports action=inspect or frame

customizations.summary: A missing Git repository is recognized from Git's message instead of only exit 128, because 'git diff' in a plain folder exits 129 with a usage warning. Under the 128-only check the diff call fell through to INTERNAL_ERROR, whose message the MCP result mapper replaces with 'Operation failed', so a folder that was never a repository was reported to the user as an lnwjud failure and retried.
Full Access attaches a new folder without prompting; stricter profiles confirm once per folder. This is the fork's deliberate approval policy.
Attach activates a project at the end of the active list only, never moves the Primary Project, and never re-activates a project the user switched off.
git_status, git_diff and git_log resolve a project from an absolute cwd instead of requiring an active workspaceId.
get_file_info reports metadata for a path without loading content, mirroring the reference tool surface this fork targets.
A goal lease from another project neither authorizes nor blocks a mutation whose workspace was actually read as unfenced; the refusal is retained when fence state cannot be confirmed.
workspace_tree honours the host explicit-absolute-read grant and invocation authorization, so it cannot refuse a path read_file accepts.

The dashboard e2e waits for the post-resize reflow before asserting the file list overflows, instead of sampling layout exactly once. Upstream's single sample intermittently read the pre-resize geometry (measured 432/432, which is deliberately non-overflowing) under whole-suite load and failed the release gate on an unrelated merge.

The fork's own release items live in the in-app What's New registry and its i18n copy. Both files conflict on nearly every upstream sync because upstream publishes the version number this fork already used locally, so resolving them by taking upstream's side deletes the fork notes while still merging, type-checking and shipping empty-state text for the fork build. Markers are version-independent values, not the version-prefixed keys that set-version and the entry rename move.

customizations.summary: The Windows tunnel-lock acceptance fixture reads this process's own creation timestamp once and reuses it. Probing it per call costs a PowerShell cold start plus a WMI query (measured 1.4-1.9s each), and three probes inside one test made the observable total 15.8s against the test's own 15s non-CI budget, so the release gate failed on fixture warmup rather than on lock behavior. Restoring the uncached probe re-introduces a load-dependent timeout that no assertion can catch.

An absolute path that belongs to no registered project is refused with the projects that exist and the folder that could be added. Upstream answers the same case with the first workspace in the registry list, which made a call read, write, audit and checkpoint inside a folder nobody named - the measured cause of work landing in the wrong project. Restoring that one-line fallback merges cleanly and reintroduces the misattribution with no failing test.

markers.contains: is not inside any registered project

customizations.summary: workspaceId is resolved as a target at the registry seam before any policy runs: an absolute host path becomes the project that owns it (active set, then registry, then host attach), a uniquely matching project name becomes its id, and a path that cannot become a project is refused with the real project list. Upstream treats the field as an opaque id, so a path or a mistyped id produced WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND and 'not an Active Project' loops across chats (measured 66 path-shaped calls and 31 WORKSPACE_NOT_FOUND completions in one log window).

When an explicit workspaceId conflicts with the project that owns the call's own absolute path, the path wins: routing rewrites workspaceId to that project and the call runs. Upstream (ed397533, 2026-10-12) refuses shell/wsl_exec/task_create/process_start outright, which measured 45 INVALID_INPUT failures in 36 hours while every Active Project was advertised as usable at the same time. The reconciled id travels to the executor, so a durable handle stays addressable by the same client.

The completed activity record carries the project a call really ran in, in both the audit row and the tailed mcp-activity.log, and the log additionally names what the caller sent as reconciledFrom. Upstream attributes every call to the workspaceId it received, so a wrong-project landing is invisible in the log and the routing fixes above cannot be measured against a fail-rate baseline. Dropping the field merges cleanly and silently removes the only evidence that path attribution works.

The durable-shell abort test gets its own 20s budget. It spawns a real detached worker and then waits with the timeout the test itself declares (5s), while Vitest's default kill is also 5s, so an honest completion can never be observed on a loaded host: measured 2394ms idle and killed at 5486ms inside the serial release suite. Restoring the missing budget argument re-creates a gate failure that no assertion can distinguish from a durable-shell regression.

markers.contains: which is a fixture budget rather than a shell-behaviour assertion

customizations.summary: The two Office bridge probes that run scripts/test-office-account-dispatch.ps1 and scripts/test-office-powerpoint-lifetime.ps1 get the same 45s per-test budget upstream already gave their sibling PowerShell probe in the same file (commit ba9d7776). The PowerShell child alone measures 5.6-7.0s on this host before Vitest adds anything, so with the 5s default these two tests cannot finish even on an idle machine and the release stage fails deterministically.

markers.contains: whose child alone costs 5.6-7.0s on this

customizations.summary: An owner-identity probe gets its own 5s per-attempt budget instead of the shared 1750ms budget meant for judging whether ANOTHER process is still alive. Windows answers 'when did this process start' only through PowerShell, whose cold start measures 1.8-2.1s on this host, so the shared budget made currentSharedActivityOwner() throw probe_timeout deterministically and the direct STDIO runtime could never publish its activity lease (its SQLite handle then blocked temp cleanup with EBUSY). The same shape blocked Desktop tunnel start: tunnel-lock.ts currentProcessOwner() inherited 1750ms, so 'Could not verify this process for the tunnel lock: probe_timeout' was a coin flip that the user worked around by killing the app and waiting for the machine to idle. Reverting either call to the single-argument form merges cleanly and re-breaks startup on any normal Windows machine.

The Windows tunnel-lock winner-order acceptance test gets 30s in local runs as well as in CI. The fixture starts six real powershell.exe processes (owner identity, the production starter script, a holder, and one mutex helper per lock operation) and each cold start measures 1.8-2.1s, making the normal instrumented cost 23.3s against upstream's 15s non-CI branch, so the stage failed deterministically with every assertion passing. Restoring the CI ternary re-breaks the release gate on any host whose PowerShell cold start is above 2.5s, and a timeout failure there is indistinguishable from a lock regression.

markers.contains: the old 15s local budget could not fit the work

customizations.summary: The first entry of active_workspace_ids is presented as the default project, never the Primary Project, because every open project is usable concurrently and the router now enforces that. Upstream ships the older key names and wording; taking its side during a merge renames the i18n keys back and leaves the components that read home.defaultProject/defaultBadge rendering missing translations.

The durable-task HTTP case grants the launched task a lifetime derived from its own 60s wall-clock allowance instead of upstream's fixed 30s. Upstream's number is shorter than the step sequence the same test runs before asserting state 'running' (measured 35s-44s on a busy Windows and macOS runner), so the durable shell expired the task exactly as declared, reported timed_out, and the assertion read that as the shell losing ownership. Linux finished inside 30s and passed, which is how the contradiction survived upstream: restoring the literal merges cleanly and re-fails CI on two of three platforms with no product defect. The ordering assertion in the same file is what makes the regression loud.

markers.contains: keeps the task lifetime above the per-case allowance so expiry cannot decide a state assertion

customizations.summary: The media_read runtime-contract fixture names its checked-in PNG absolutely through import.meta.url instead of upstream's cwd-relative '.test-assets/media-read.png'. media_read resolves a relative path against the harness workspace root, which falls back to the process working directory, so upstream's string only resolved when the suite ran from packages/mcp-server and failed with FILE_NOT_FOUND from the repository root - the directory CI uses - on Windows, macOS and Linux at the same step. Restoring the relative literal merges cleanly and re-breaks the native platform contract stage.

lnwjud records, per MCP call, which listener the server itself observed (local_stdio for the STDIO runtime, loopback_http for the loopback MCP endpoint) and call_history returns that recorded value instead of hardcoding 'unknown' for every row. Upstream ships the transport enum, the IPC validation, the tool filter and the renderer's timing column but no producer, so a filter on any transport always yields an empty page that a remote agent reads as a connector outage. Reverting any marker here silently restores the stub: upstream owns all of these files, so a merge that keeps the upstream side removes the attribution while typecheck and CI still pass.

markers.contains: an empty secure_tunnel or external_mcp result is not evidence that the connector is down

customizations.summary: Upstream owns .github/workflows/ci.yml and its on.push.branches list only main, dev and release/v*. This fork develops on master, so without the extra master entry hosted CI never runs for fork work - the exact silent condition found on 2026-10-16, where every fork commit had total_count = 0 check-runs. The fork also re-emits the native suite failure lines as ::error:: check annotations, because job and run logs return 403 without repository admin and the public check-runs annotations API is the only evidence channel available; dropping that block restores an unobservable 'Process completed with exit code 1'. Accepting the upstream side of this file during a merge therefore removes both the trigger and the failure evidence while every local test still passes.

Upstream resolves FFmpeg/ffprobe for Windows screen_record with Get-Command (PATH only) and the mcp-server media seam falls back to a bare executable name, so a freshly imaged machine reports 'ffmpeg is not installed; install ffmpeg' even though every Windows installer in this fork ships resources/media-runtime/ffmpeg.exe (the afterPack evidence hook asserts it). The fork instead resolves the bundled runtime first - from the bridge script's own resources directory in PowerShell, and from process.resourcesPath or the directory beside process.execPath in TypeScript - and reports the searched bundled locations when it truly is missing. Accepting the upstream side of windows-capability-bridge.ps1 or upgrade-runtime.ts during a sync silently restores the PATH-only lookup and re-breaks screen_record and video media_read on clean machines, which local tests on a developer workstation with ffmpeg installed cannot catch.
